title: Setting Up the PAM

patient.name: Mr Goh Teck Seng
patient.presenting_complaint: Referred for a Potential Acuity Meter test before cataract surgery

history.hpc: Mr Goh says 'Doctor want to check what is my vision can become after operation.' He has a cataract and the doctor has ordered a PAM. This station focuses on performing the test with correct preparation and technique.
history.pmhx: Cataract. No diabetes. No known macular disease.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Cataract present; the OT must ensure adequate dilation before testing

pam_technique.principle: PAM projects a Snellen chart directly onto the retina, bypassing the cataract, to predict potential post-operative acuity
pam_technique.preparation: Pupil dilation is required; confirm the eye is adequately dilated before testing
pam_technique.steps: Confirm identity and eye, set up and align the machine, instruct the patient to read the smallest line they can see, repeat to confirm
pam_technique.result_right: Predicted potential acuity recorded as the best line read reliably

diagnosis: The PAM is performed with correct preparation and technique: the pupil is confirmed dilated, the patient is correctly positioned and aligned, and the best reliably-read line is recorded as the predicted potential acuity. The result is reported to the doctor. This station emphasises correct test setup rather than a single clinical outcome.

immediate: Confirm identity and the correct eye against the order
Confirm the pupil is adequately dilated — required for PAM
Explain the test simply and gain cooperation
Set up and align the PAM correctly at the chinrest
Instruct the patient to read the smallest visible line and repeat to confirm reliability
Record the predicted acuity and report it to the doctor
follow_up: Doctor to use the result in surgical counselling
Repeat or escalate if a reliable reading cannot be obtained
patient_education: Explain the test estimates vision after the cataract is removed
Reassure the test is quick and painless
Explain dilation will blur near vision for a few hours

key_points: Confirms identity and the correct eye
Confirms the order and the purpose of the test
Confirms the pupil is dilated as required
Explains the test to the patient
Sets up and aligns the PAM correctly
Repeats the reading to confirm reliability
Understands the PAM principle (projecting a chart past the cataract)
Knows dilation is required before testing
Reports the result to the doctor without making the surgical decision
Knows to repeat if the reading is unreliable
Documents the result and the eye
Educates the patient on the test and dilation
